UU Nomor 45 Tahun 2009
UU Nomor 45 Tahun 2009 is a legislative law and formal legal regulation issued by the Republic of Indonesia that serves as the primary legal framework for the nation’s aquatic and fisheries sectors. Enacted in 2009, this statute establishes the general provisions and principles for the management and utilization of Indonesia's fish resources. Its core purpose is to ensure the sustainability of aquatic resources while providing comprehensive protections for both maritime and inland water systems. This legislation acts as an amendment to Undang-Undang Nomor 31 Tahun 2004, providing a comprehensive framework for fishery business operations, including fishing operations, aquaculture, and fish farming. The scope of the law covers a broad spectrum of activities, including trade regulations and the establishment of requirements for business and investment licenses within the fisheries sector. Furthermore, it contains specific provisions regarding the handling, processing, and quality standards of fish, notably those outlined in Article 25A and various specific legal articles such as Pasal 100D.

Additionally, UU Nomor 45 Tahun 2009 governs the logistical and administrative aspects of the maritime industry, including the registration of fishing vessels, the issuance of sailing permits, and the management of fishery ports. The law specifically defines the duties and authority of the Syahbandar (harbor master) at these locations and establishes formal legal provisions for fishery levies and the specific duties of fishery supervisors. To ensure regulatory enforcement, the law provides a framework for criminal procedures, judicial processes, and legal penalties within the fisheries sector. This includes the establishment of a fishery court and specific court sub-units, as well as defining the authority and powers of investigators tasked with handling fishery-related crimes and judicial procedures.

Furthermore, the identifier UU Nomor 45 Tahun 2009 is also associated with a legal document containing regulations regarding the Indonesian prosecution system. Kapal Perikanan refers to maritime vessels, ships, boats, or other floating tools utilized for a diverse range of activities within the fisheries sector. These activities encompass fish capture, support operations for fish capture, fish cultivation, transportation of fish, and fish processing. Furthermore, Kapal Perikanan may be utilized for fisheries training, as well as for fisheries research and exploration purposes.

In the context of Indonesian maritime regulations, Kapal Perikanan can specifically denote a fishing vessel owned by Indonesian citizens that operates both within Indonesian waters and on the high seas. To operate legally, such a vessel must obtain a fitness certificate, which is a mandatory prerequisite for receiving a sailing permit. This sailing permit must be secured before the vessel can engage in catching or transporting fish from a fishing port.

Additionally, Kapal Perikanan serves as a functional location where fishery supervisors can perform their official duties. Within the framework of fishery legislation, Nelayan Kecil are granted several regulatory benefits and exemptions. These include exemptions from specific license requirements, certain vessel monitoring requirements, and the fishery levy. Furthermore, they qualify for various other regulatory exemptions as stipulated by law.

While they are granted these exemptions, Nelayan Kecil are still subject to the rule of law and may face legal penalties for violating specific articles of the legislation. Specifically, Peraturan Menteri details the procedures and conditions required for license issuance and provides the technical specifications for the registration of fishing vessels. They also encompass the definition of administrative and technical requirements necessary for various industry operations.

Furthermore, these regulations cover the standards for fishery product quality and identify the specific types of fishing equipment that are prohibited. Peraturan Menteri also establishes the framework for administrative sanctions and outlines the functional positions and responsibilities of fishery supervisors.<SEP>A ministerial regulation that provides detailed guidelines for the execution of duties by fishery supervisors.

Ayat (1)
Ayat (1) is a structural designation in Indonesian legal texts representing the first paragraph or first clause of various articles (Pasal) across different legislative frameworks. Because it serves as a recurring structural label, the name refers to several distinct legal provisions and definitions depending on the specific article in which it appears.

In maritime and fishing regulations, Ayat (1) of Pasal 9 specifies the prohibition of harmful fishing tools. Separately, Ayat (1) of Pasal 25C provides a formal definition of the fishery industry, stating that it includes the provision of capture facilities and fishery processing.

The designation also applies to other specific legal requirements and procedural rules. It serves as the first paragraph of Pasal 28, the first paragraph of the amended Pasal 44, and a specific paragraph within Pasal 65. Furthermore, Ayat (1) is identified as the first paragraph of Pasal 48 within the context of UU Nomor 45 Tahun 2009.

In other legal contexts, Ayat (1) functions as a subsection of Pasal 76B, which defines the conditions for auctioning evidence, and as the first clause of Article 27.

Ayat (2)
Ayat (2) refers to a designation used for various second paragraphs or clauses across different legal articles and legislative frameworks. Because this term is used in multiple contexts, it represents several distinct provisions depending on the specific law or article being referenced.

In one instance, Ayat (2) of Pasal 9 specifies that the detailed rules associated with that section are governed by ministerial regulations. It is also identified as the second paragraph of Pasal 28 and the second paragraph of Pasal 48 within the legislative framework of UU Nomor 45 Tahun 2009.

Furthermore, Ayat (2) refers to the second paragraph or subsection of Article 66 and the second paragraph of Article 23. In other contexts, it corresponds to the second clause of Pasal 25C, which is characterized as being sufficiently clear, as well as the second clause of Article 27. More generally, it is described as a specific paragraph or clause within a legal document that is stated as being sufficiently clear.

Penjelasan Resmi
Penjelasan Resmi is the formal official explanation or commentary provided within a legal or legislative framework. It functions as a dedicated section within a legal document, legislative document, or a piece of legislation specifically intended to clarify the specific laws or provisions contained therein. As a core component of a legal structure, Penjelasan Resmi serves as the official explanation section of a law or legal statute, providing the clarifying text associated with the legislation.

Furthermore, Penjelasan Resmi encompasses the official explanations provided specifically for regulations. By serving as an authoritative guide, it ensures that the meaning, intent, and application of the legal requirements are clearly communicated within the context of the relevant official documentation. It provides essential context and clarification for specific regulations, ensuring that the underlying objectives of the legal documents are accurately conveyed.

In practical application, Penjelasan Resmi represents the official explanation associated with various legal documents. A specific instance of this is the official explanation section associated with UU Nomor 45 Tahun 2009.<SEP>The official explanation associated with UU Nomor 45 Tahun 2009.<SEP>The official explanation section of a legal document.
